-  # Build-only — `#[test]` needs the std harness, so tests run in the `check` job.
+  # The no_std proof: build the no_std-capable crates for a bare-metal target (no std

   no-std:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     defaults:
@@ -81,10 +83,14 @@ jobs:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v6
       - name: Toolchain + bare-metal target
         run: rustup show && rustup target add thumbv7em-none-eabi
-      - name: Build no_std (pure)

         run: cargo build -p trussbars-core --no-default-features --target thumbv7em-none-eabi

@@ -8,7 +8,19 @@ license.workspace = true
 keywords = ["template", "maxbars", "parser", "codegen"]
 categories = ["template-engine", "parser-implementations"]
 
-# A build-time library (the proc-macro depends on it); std, no runtime deps yet.
+# The front-end (lexer → parser → desugar) needs only `alloc`, so it is
+# `no_std`-capable for the VM on bare-metal/WASM. The emitter (build-time codegen,
+# used only by the proc-macro / dev CLIs) stays behind `std`.
+[features]
+default = ["std"]
+# `std` also gates the `emit` module (it uses `f64::round`/`fract`, std-only). The
+# parse path builds with `--no-default-features` for `no_std` + `alloc`.
+std = []
+
+# The dev CLI drives the std-only `emit`, so it needs `std`.
+[[bin]]
+name = "truss-emit"
+required-features = ["std"]
 
 [lints]
 workspace = true

@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 [package]
 name = "trussbars-vm"
-description = "The Trussbars VM backend (spike): a dynamic-Value tree-walk interpreter for MaxBars, reusing the trussbars-template front-end. Serves dynamic/runtime templates; docs/11. Lenient mode only in this spike."
+description = "The Trussbars VM backend (spike): a dynamic-Value tree-walk interpreter for MaxBars, reusing the trussbars-template front-end. Serves dynamic/runtime templates; docs/11. no_std-capable (alloc) so the VM can ship to embedded/WASM."
 version.workspace = true
 edition.workspace = true
 rust-version.workspace = true
@@ -9,10 +9,24 @@ keywords = ["template", "maxbars", "interpreter", "vm"]
 categories = ["template-engine"]
 
 [dependencies]
-trussbars-template = { path = "../trussbars-template" }
-trussbars-core = { path = "../trussbars-core" }
+# Front-end + runtime, no_std-capable (their `std` is turned on by ours below).
+trussbars-template = { path = "../trussbars-template", default-features = false }
+trussbars-core = { path = "../trussbars-core", default-features = false }
+# `no_std` f64 floor (identical to `f64::floor`; used by the `round` helper).
+libm = "0.2"
 # Used only by the `truss-vm` dev CLI (JSON data → Value); the library is JSON-agnostic.
-serde_json = "1"
+serde_json = { version = "1", optional = true }
+
+[features]
+default = ["std"]
+# `std` pulls the dev-CLI JSON dep and turns on the dependencies' std + the ECMA-f64
+# `perf` formatter (so the std VM is byte-identical to the oracle). `--no-default-features`
+# is the `no_std` + `alloc` build (f64 falls back to `Display`, the documented divergence).
+std = ["serde_json", "trussbars-core/std", "trussbars-core/perf", "trussbars-template/std"]
+
+[[bin]]
+name = "truss-vm"
+required-features = ["std"]
 
 [lints]
 workspace = true

@@ -46,7 +46,7 @@ What this buys, and what it costs, stated plainly:
 | **Injection-safe (no SSTI)** | ✅ no interpreter at all | ✅ **preserved** — static names rule (§6); no `apply`, no computed partials, no computed `lookup` |
 | **Host-typed field checking** (`{{post.titlee}}` ⇒ compile error) | ✅ rustc-enforced | ⚠️ lost in lenient mode; **recovered in AOT-compat mode** (§7), exact for the modeled subset |
 | **Performance** | safe-Rust ceiling (~0.8 µs, docs/05) | interpreter — 10–100× slower; still expected to beat handlebars, nowhere near AOT |
-| **`no_std` + `forbid(unsafe)`** | ✅ | ✅ target (the value model is `alloc`-only; see §5) |
+| **`no_std` + `forbid(unsafe)`** | ✅ | ✅ **shipped** — the VM lib (+ the `trussbars-template` parse path it reuses) builds `--no-default-features` for bare-metal/WASM; `alloc`-only, `forbid(unsafe)` (see §5). The dev `truss-vm` CLI stays `std`. |
 
 The host-typed-checking loss is the real trade. It is the *same* trade Tera/minijinja
 make against Askama/Maud — Trussbars now spans both halves of that split deliberately,
